evidence.positive: Created a two-procedure case in demo-demo (p-colorectal + p-arthroscopy-knee, case 41094, operation 01a044af-68b2-7871-bb82-c744dc751c3c) and hit GET /api/admin/patients/{pmrn}/operations/41094/antibiotic-candidates, which invalidates the cache and re-runs resolve(). Response: outcome RECOMMENDED, recommended [["CEFAZOLIN","METRONIDAZOLE"]]. Per-option statuses show colorectal's CEFAZOLIN+METRONIDAZOLE as RECOMMENDED while colorectal's CEFTRIAXONE+METRONIDAZOLE and the knee's bare CEFAZOLIN are both NOT_SELECTED - the wider configured regimen covered the narrower one it contains, and only a configured option was offered. A second pair (p-appendectomy CEFAZOLIN+METRONIDAZOLE + p-arthroscopy-knee CEFAZOLIN, case 95358) gave the same result. Two further ticket bullets checked on the same build: p-gastro-uncomplicated + p-arthroscopy-knee returned RECOMMENDED [["CEFAZOLIN"]] rather than optional (optionality is per procedure), and with anaphylaxis allergies to a-cefazolin and m-vancomycin-iv on a colorectal+knee case (44243) the knee lost every option and the case returned ALL_CONTRAINDICATED, not SUPPRESSED_DISAGREEMENT, even though colorectal still had CEFTRIAXONE+METRONIDAZOLE available.
evidence.negative: Created a case whose two procedures share no covering option (p-arthroscopy-knee offering CEFAZOLIN, p-eus-fna-cystic-lesion offering CEFTRIAXONE, case 55340, operation 01a044af-68f6-78d4-be53-b9931c4f29ba) and hit the same endpoint. Response: outcome SUPPRESSED_DISAGREEMENT, recommended []. Every option on both procedures came back NOT_SELECTED. No synthesized CEFAZOLIN+CEFTRIAXONE regimen appeared, confirming the case suppresses rather than combining two procedures' needs into a regimen nobody wrote. Application log for that operation: 'Operation 01a044af-68f6-78d4-be53-b9931c4f29ba has procedures whose surviving options do not overlap - suppressing recommendation'.
evidence.red_check: Ran a pre-fix build of the changed class in the container. First a control: recompiled the shipped source unchanged (only @Slf4j replaced with an explicit org.slf4j logger, since lombok is not on the runtime classpath) with javac against /app/jib-classpath-file, copied it into /app/classes, restarted - positive case still RECOMMENDED [["CEFAZOLIN","METRONIDAZOLE"]], so the recompile itself is behaviour-neutral. Then the un-fix: reverted covers() from drugs.containsAll(drugsOf(covered)) to drugs.equals(drugsOf(covered)), which is the pre-fix exact-drug-set intersection, compiled and installed it, restarted. The positive case (41094) went red - outcome flipped from RECOMMENDED to SUPPRESSED_DISAGREEMENT, recommended became [], colorectal's CEFAZOLIN+METRONIDAZOLE dropped from RECOMMENDED to NOT_SELECTED, and the log emitted 'Operation 01a044af-68b2-7871-bb82-c744dc751c3c has procedures whose surviving options do not overlap - suppressing recommendation' for the first and only time. Restored: copied the backed-up shipped classes back over /app/classes and restarted; all five class-file md5s match the originals exactly (ProcedureAntibioticCandidateService.class c305117c8e0c6336f2041a92c9bf84fd, $1 f95c3962c35eaf9fe1161f4c4ca1b73f, $CaseSurvivors f136824d14fc9ddc5c711f3926fefe49, $ProcedurePathways 6cb29ca5c7f2d3c14e058a91634662fe, $Walk 6f68629cbab5a479298278725facdc66), and the positive case re-ran to RECOMMENDED [["CEFAZOLIN","METRONIDAZOLE"]].

caveats: The pre-fix class was produced by reverting covers() to exact-set equality in the current source rather than compiling the literal parent commit, because the parent predates the Walk/acuity refactor and no longer compiles against main.

Evidence was read from GET /api/admin/patients/{pmrn}/operations/{caseId}/antibiotic-candidates, which calls explain() -> resolve() and returns the real AntibioticResolution; the downstream guidance alert and clinical UI that consume that resolution were not exercised.
Only the demo-demo tenant's shipped pathway configuration was used; mayo and mgb configurations were not exercised.
Cases with a ProcedureCombinationPathway written for the procedure pair take a different service and were not exercised.

automation.assessment: Coverage is already strong and does not need adding to. AntibioticResolutionSpecTest (added with the change) holds 40 tests that pin every bullet in the ticket by name - mp01-mp20 for the multi-procedure coverage rules and n01-n19 for the negatives, including 'regimensThatMerelyOverlapCoverNeither', 'aProcedureSurvivingNothingDecidesTheCase', 'oneProcedureSurvivingNothingIsContraindicationNotDisagreement', 'oneMandatingProcedureMakesTheCaseNotOptional' and 'anOptionCoveringOnlyOneProcedureDrops'. AntibioticPathwayResolutionSpecTest covers the single-procedure walk. Duplicating any of that at the e2e level would buy nothing. The only thing not pinned anywhere is that a multi-procedure resolution survives the round trip through the cached-resolution path and the admin debugger view, which is what this validation exercised by hand.
proposed_tests: qa-suite: a multi-procedure demo case (p-colorectal + p-arthroscopy-knee) asserting the antibiotic-candidates endpoint returns outcome RECOMMENDED with the single CEFAZOLIN+METRONIDAZOLE option and the knee's bare CEFAZOLIN marked NOT_SELECTED.
qa-suite: a non-covering pair (p-arthroscopy-knee + p-eus-fna-cystic-lesion) asserting outcome SUPPRESSED_DISAGREEMENT with an empty recommendation and no combined regimen.

jira_comment:
Verdict: deploy-ready.

Positive: A colorectal plus knee arthroscopy case resolved to the single wider configured regimen, cefazolin with metronidazole, with the narrower bare-cefazolin option correctly dropped.
Negative: A knee arthroscopy plus EUS-FNA case, where no configured option covers both, returned no recommendation and suppressed rather than inventing a combined regimen.
Red check: Reverting the coverage test to the old exact-match comparison and swapping the recompiled class into the running app flipped the positive case to suppressed with an empty recommendation; the shipped class was restored and the case returned to recommending cefazolin with metronidazole.

Automation: Forty unit tests already pin every rule in this ticket by name, so nothing new is needed beyond two optional end-to-end checks through the antibiotic-candidates endpoint.
